- Private (VPC/on-prem): full network isolation + customer-managed keys, best for strict regulatory requirements.

Hi Samantha / Raj — thanks for the questions. Quick technical reply below; happy to review in the workshop and share logs/examples.

1) Noisy neighbor — what to expect - In shared (hosted) environments resource contention can show up as increased tail latency (p99) during noisy periods. For retail workloads, this often correlates with sudden spikes (e.g., marketing campaign or cart-abandonment wave). Typical impact we observe on shared pools without request-level QoS: p50 stays stable, p95 increases ~25–50ms, p99 can jump by 100–300ms during extreme contention windows. We mitigate this via continuous batching, admission control, and smart routing but residual tail risk exists.

2) Dedicated — isolation & SLAs - Dedicated capacity provides an isolated pool of GPUs and scheduler-level isolation. Practically this means: predictable concurrency and per-token throughput without interference from other tenants. Our Dedicated offering includes SLA targets: 99.9% uptime and p99 latency targets per model family (SLA PDF attached). We also provide an option for reserved burst nodes to absorb traffic spikes.

3) Migration path (Hosted -> Dedicated) - Migration is designed to be low-friction: same API surface, model version pinning, and canary rollout support. Typical plan:
  - Provision Dedicated pool sized from a short load test (we can run a 24–48h pilot).
  - Deploy the same model version with identical quantization and runtime config.
  - Gradual traffic cutover via weighted routing (canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%).
  - Rollback: instant traffic weight flip back to Hosted variant; no model re-training required.
  - Downtime: usually none; most customers see negligible user-facing downtime if canary steps are followed.

4) Caveats and things to watch - Large context models and KV cache sizes affect memory and batching efficiency; Dedicated sizing must account for worst-case sequence lengths.
- Quantization differences can slightly affect latency/throughput; we validate parity during pilot.
- SLOs are model-family specific (e.g., gpt-like vs. small chat models) — we'll map your models to our performance profiles in the workshop.

5) Recommendations for Acme - Given your peaks (~120 rps) and strict PII needs, Dedicated looks like the safer path: it gives infra-level isolation and SLA coverage while keeping predictable unit economics. If you want to defer commitment, start on Hosted with request-level QoS and a short Dedicated pilot to validate sizing before Black Friday.
